disposition_mapping.rationale: Extraction and closing-rate retranslation are mechanical once sources and rates are defined, so the step moves to automated connectors wherever feeds are reliable. The council's strongest round-2 convergence (emerging_economy, finance_domain, hitl_designer, agentic_architect) rejected treating manual extraction as a shrinking exception queue: for sites with PDF bank statements, legacy subledgers or intermittent connectivity, manual extraction is retained as a permanently supported, equally compliant mode, not a deprecated branch. ACR-R-01 and ACR-R-07 bind here: the risk-rating schedule and closing exchange rates remain mandatory inputs to both modes, and KB-07's closing-rate requirement cannot be waived for any account on efficiency grounds.

Matching is restructured toward governed automation but deliberately kept as its own step boundary, rejecting maximalist's fusion with extraction. Pragmatist, finance_domain, accounting_standards, agentic_architect and emerging_economy converged that a feed-load failure and a matching disagreement are distinct failure modes with distinct owners, and that the auto-match rule set is itself a KB-06 policy decision requiring versioned change control rather than silent tuning. ACR-R-02 is satisfied by the matching function surviving with an explicit manual path for non-standardised data, and intercompany tagging is preserved per KB-14.

Near-unanimous council position: investigation and classification is irreducible judgment work under KB-02 and KB-05 and must not be delegated to auto-classification with human rubber-stamping. The step is kept distinct from both matching and JE preparation (rejecting accounting_standards' and maximalist's full-merge proposals) because a controller/auditor needs to see what the accountant decided an item was before seeing what they decided to book. AI tooling may suggest, but the classification and its evidential basis remain accountable to the named GL accountant, satisfying ACR-R-03.

Preparation and sign-off are merged into one step because they are performed by the same actor with no real handoff, consistent with hitl_designer, agentic_architect, finance_domain and emerging_economy's convergence that the step-boundary is overhead. The prior-period error record remains a mandatory input and prior-period errors continue to be corrected retrospectively rather than netted, satisfying ACR-R-04 and ACR-R-06 and KB-05. Estimation-based entries retain a documented human basis per KB-04/KB-10.

Council round 2 decisively rejected maximalist's elimination of sign-off: pragmatist, finance_domain, accounting_standards, hitl_designer and agentic_architect all held that a passive system timestamp is not equivalent to an affirmative human attestation, and KB-02's evidential-trail requirement depends on the latter. The step boundary is removed as ceremonial, but the function survives as a discrete, separately logged attestation event inside TS-04, distinct from the draft-generation event — satisfying the spirit of the unconstrained-by-design latitude without dissolving the underlying control.

Reviewer approval survives for every account (ACR-R-09), restructured to risk-weighted intensity so the reviewer's attention concentrates on exceptions, overrides and estimation entries. Following pragmatist, hitl_designer and accounting_standards against finance_domain's/maximalist's auto-certification proposal, no account class is permitted to bypass human reviewer visibility entirely — existence of review, not merely its intensity, is what the requirement protects. Actor separation from TS-04 (ACR-R-05) is preserved architecturally, not just procedurally.

This is explicitly unconstrained by design, and the council's round-2 convergence (hitl_designer, accounting_standards, and agentic_architect's concession) favoured treating the escalation decision — not merely detection — as a controller judgment exercised at the same moment, with the same evidence, as the approval decision itself, rather than a pre-dispatched automated action the controller audits afterward. Ageing-threshold detection is mechanical and system-flagged, but deciding whether/how/to whom to escalate is folded into TS-05. The escalation log is preserved as a distinct, separately traceable output to satisfy finance_domain's and emerging_economy's concern that the function not lose visibility inside a general 'approved' status, and batch-mode operation is retained for low-connectivity sites.

Evidence retention and status reporting survive (ACR-R-08) but move from a batch, after-the-fact compilation to incremental, near-real-time capture as upstream steps complete, which better serves KB-02's evidential-trail requirement than evidence reconstructed from memory under close-timetable pressure. A named accountable GL accountant remains responsible for resolving incomplete or flagged evidence packages rather than the function being reduced to 'the system logs it somewhere,' per pragmatist's and hitl_designer's objections, and hybrid/local storage options are retained per emerging_economy's data-residency concern.

steps.description: GL, bank, subledger and third-party balances are extracted for every in-scope account due under its risk-rated frequency. Source systems with stable feeds are pulled by automated connectors; sources without reliable connectivity (correspondent-bank PDFs, legacy subledgers, intermittent-connectivity sites) are extracted through a permanently supported manual/semi-manual path, selected per source system, not a deprecated fallback. Both paths must consume the reconciliation schedule by account risk rating and closing exchange rates, and must retranslate foreign-currency balances at the closing rate for every multi-currency account. If a feed is unavailable, a rate is stale, or retranslation fails, that account's extraction halts and raises a visible exception (with batch/async notification supported for low-connectivity sites) rather than substituting a default.
inputs: Reconciliation schedule by account risk rating
steps.name: Balance extraction and FX retranslation (automated and manual first-class paths)

steps.description: Transactions are matched between the GL and the comparison source. Rules-based automated matching handles standardised, high-volume items with a logged rule citation per match, reversible on review; a permanently supported manual matching path handles accounts with inconsistent or non-standardised data. Matching remains a step distinct from extraction so a feed-load failure and a matching disagreement are diagnosable as different failure modes with different owners. The auto-match rule set and tolerance thresholds are centrally governed, versioned and subject to change control, never tuned silently by a local administrator or tool default. Intercompany-tagged items remain separately identifiable through both the automated and manual paths.
steps.name: Transaction matching (governed automation with manual exception path)

steps.description: Unmatched items are investigated, explained, supported with evidence and classified by the named GL accountant. Decision-support tooling may retrieve similar historical items and draft a candidate classification and explanation, but the classification decision and its evidential basis must originate from and be owned by the accountant, not be an opaque auto-generated label the accountant is nudged to accept. Items identified as intercompany or estimation-related (NRV, provisioning, ECL-adjacent) are explicitly tagged for downstream routing.
steps.name: Investigate and classify reconciling items (decision-supported)

steps.description: Adjusting journal entries are prepared for items requiring correction, with the prior-period error record consumed as a mandatory input so prior-period errors are corrected retrospectively, never netted into the current period. Mechanical reclass entries may be system-drafted; estimation-based entries (NRV write-downs, provisions, ECL-type adjustments) must be human-authored with a documented basis. This step merges the former separate sign-off step but preserves it as a distinct, separately logged internal event: a draft-generation event followed by an explicit, individually attributable preparer attestation ('I prepared/reviewed this; here is the basis') that is not inferred from a system submission timestamp. The preparer of this step is always a different actor from the reviewer in TS-05.
steps.name: Prepare adjusting journal entries and preparer attestation

steps.description: An independent reviewer, distinct from the preparer, reviews and approves the reconciliation and its adjusting entries. Review intensity is risk-weighted: full line-level review for accounts with exceptions, overrides, estimation entries or elevated risk rating; lighter sampled or batch-confirmation review for fully auto-matched, exception-free low-risk accounts. Every account receives a human-visible confirmation each period — no account class bypasses reviewer visibility entirely — and the threshold defining 'lighter review' is owned and periodically re-validated by the controller, never the preparer or a tool default. Items crossing the ageing threshold are flagged automatically by the system, but the decision of whether, how and to whom to escalate remains a controller-owned judgment exercised at the point of review, using the evidence already assembled; the resulting escalation log is retained as a distinct, separately traceable output. Review and escalation support both continuous/dashboard and periodic batch operation so entities without continuous connectivity or centralised, time-zone-aligned review capacity remain compliant.
steps.name: Risk-based reviewer approval and aged-item escalation

steps.description: Reconciliation evidence — matched and unmatched items, explanations, JE drafts and attestations, approvals, and the escalation log — is captured incrementally as each upstream step completes and auto-packaged into the system of record, with hybrid or local storage options where cloud-only retention is infeasible for data-residency or licensing reasons. Status reporting is near-real-time rather than compiled retroactively. Incomplete, overdue or flagged reconciliations are surfaced to an accountable GL accountant for resolution, not silently logged.
steps.name: Evidence retention and status reporting
